Raj / Procurement — thanks for joining the thread. Attaching our standard MSA and DPA templates to give you both something concrete to review. Highlights and expected negotiation items we typically see: 
- Data residency & processing: customers want to ensure specific regions and subprocessor lists — we can provide a region-lock option and SCCs for EU customers.
- Indemnity / liability caps: we are typically able to negotiate to Xx monthly/annual cap tied to committed spend; we can share precedent language.
- Security & audit rights: we provide SOC 2 Type II report and can discuss limited audit windows.

Hannah, Dylan — hop in with any technical notes for Raj that would be helpful up front. Raj — can you confirm preferred channel (DocuSign) and an internal SLA so we can set expectations in the deal plan?

Attachments: MSA_v1_ACME_marked.docx (attached), DPA-template.pdf (attached)

Best — Marissa

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap + next steps from today — stakeholders & legal routing

Hi Raj / team — quick technical notes to help procurement/legal triage: 

1) Data residency: Redwood supports region pinning for inference workloads; customer can restrict model serving to a specific cloud region (e.g., us-west-2). We can provide an exportable subprocessor list and support KMS integrations for customer-controlled keys.

2) Telemetry/usage: Redwood collects aggregated telemetry for product health (latency, error rates). We do not use customer prompts for model training. Telemetry is pseudonymized and shared only at aggregate levels; we can remove telemetry retention on request per contract.

3) SOC 2: we will share our SOC 2 Type II report in the next email (security portal link).

If you want, I can add two short bullets to the MSA (data residency & telemetry usage) and highlight them in the DocuSign envelope.

— Hannah, Solutions Engineer
